label: Bible Study
prompt: And Samson called unto the LORD, and said, O Lord GOD, remember me, I pray thee, and _____ me, I pray thee, only this once, O God, that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes.
verse: And Samson called unto the LORD, and said, O Lord GOD, remember me, I pray thee, and strengthen me, I pray thee, only this once, O God, that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes.
note: Samson's last prayer, in the temple of Dagon — eyes gone, hair growing back, one more push left.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open unto their _____: but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil.
verse: For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open unto their prayers: but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil.
note: God's eyes are on the righteous and His ears are open to their prayers — watching and listening.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And Jesus answering said, A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among _____, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
verse: And Jesus answering said, A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
note: The Good Samaritan story begins on the Jericho road, with a man who fell among thieves and was left half dead.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Deep calleth unto deep at the noise of thy _____: all thy waves and thy billows are gone over me.
verse: Deep calleth unto deep at the noise of thy waterspouts: all thy waves and thy billows are gone over me.
note: The psalmist, far from Jerusalem near the Jordan's headwaters, feels the waves of trouble rolling over him.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Thou tellest my _____: put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book?
verse: Thou tellest my wanderings: put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book?
note: God tallies every one of David's 'wanderings' and keeps his tears in a bottle — the most tender filing system in Scripture.
